market_scope: US-listed semiconductor and AI data center infrastructure stocks only

china_a_shares.reason: Excluded because filing comparability and source confidence are below the US-market screen threshold.

safe_harbor: Educational information only. Not financial advice. Prices can move materially around earnings.

quote_source.name: Yahoo Finance and Reuters market snapshots
quote_source.note: August 21 regular closes are used where August 24 trading was not final. KLAC, MU, AMAT, PDFS, and TSM include August 24 intraday or pre-market observations.

market_emotion.basis: SOXX lost about 7% from August 18 through August 21, technology shares remained soft on August 24, and NVIDIA, Marvell, and Broadcom earnings create concentrated event risk. The pullback improves entry prices, but only filing-backed names with valuation support qualify for staged buys.

strict_scoring.score_formula: forward fundamental surprise + narrative and expectation shift + supply-chain moat and diffusion + valuation and reaction gap + financial quality and positioning risk + evidence integrity
strict_scoring.interpretation: The score is an ordinal research rank, not a calibrated probability, target return, or backtested alpha estimate.
hard_gates: fresh attributable filing or company evidence
no unresolved accounting or liquidity red flag
valuation and market reaction assessed against expectations
buy list may be empty when no candidate reaches 82

position_sizing_overlay.rule: Use the conviction rank only for selection. Size is reduced independently for volatility, portfolio correlation, crowding, customer concentration, liquidity, and imminent earnings risk.
position_sizing_overlay.initial_size: about one-quarter of intended exposure for current staged buys
position_sizing_overlay.exit_rule: Review or exit when the guidance, demand, margin, cash-flow, or supply-chain thesis breaks; do not rely on price stops alone.

AVGO.reason: AI semiconductor revenue accelerated 143%, free cash flow reached $10.3B, and valuation plus drawdown leave room for underreaction; the September 2 report must validate the forward narrative and limits size.

KLAC.reason: Process-control intensity, double-digit growth, strong free cash flow, and a large drawdown versus filing strength create the cleanest reaction-gap setup, despite a still-full multiple.

LRCX.reason: Revenue and earnings growth are excellent, but the post-earnings rerating offers less entry margin than KLAC.

AMAT.reason: Fiscal Q3 growth and DRAM exposure are strong, but price and expectations remain elevated after the AI equipment rerating.

FORM.reason: HBM and CPO test intensity drove a major earnings inflection, but the stock has more than doubled year to date.

NVDA.reason: Exceptional platform quality is offset by an August 26 binary event and power/site constraints outside NVIDIA's control.

MU.reason: HBM and memory earnings are extraordinary, but the roughly 239% year-to-date rise leaves substantial cyclical and positioning risk.

PDFS.reason: Q2 passed the profit and cash-flow gate, but valuation and integration risk prevent a current best-buy rating.

CRDO.reason: AEC and connectivity exposure are attractive, but momentum, expectations, and valuation are demanding.

MRVL.reason: The Google custom-silicon agreement validates demand, but concentration, valuation, a large year-to-date gain, and August 27 earnings make entry asymmetric.

rankings.positioning: Quarter-size starter positions only; add after earnings confirmation or support retests.

NVDA.status: Quality passes; August 26 earnings must be cleared before entry.

MU.status: Fundamentals pass; price-cycle discipline fails today's buy gate.

source_intelligence.signal: Supplier-side AI exposure remains favored as hyperscaler capital expenditure rises above $1.2T on a 12-month view.
Photonics, HBM, build-to-print equipment capacity, and public power/water constraints are moving to the foreground.
Accelerator economics must be modeled with HBM, wafer starts, packaging yields, networking, and customer deployment capacity.
Institutional research remains bullish on key AI suppliers, while financing and capacity headlines raise selectivity.
Order activity improved; generative AI, CoWoS constraints, foundry momentum, and subcontractor gains remain supportive.
HBM supply is expected to stay tight through 2027, with 50%-60% bit growth potentially insufficient for demand.
Training compute is scaling faster than power and data movement, elevating ASICs, HBM, photonics, and integration.
Rubin-class racks expose the physical bill of materials: liquid cooling, 800G networking, DPUs, storage, and power shelves.
Third-party infrastructure capital, GPU-initiated storage, and powered-site development are becoming explicit enablers.
NVIDIA earnings are a market catalyst; Google's Marvell agreement validates custom silicon but adds customer-concentration risk.
Semiconductors entered a high-event-risk week with technology shares weak and NVIDIA, Marvell, and Broadcom reports ahead.
